reviews.body: One real bug (fixed now?) and a reply to Frank.
Nice work on the spreadsheet check.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: FX is exactly where you want Decimal. Integer micro-rates and hand-written rounding feels fragile; `Decimal(amount) * Decimal(rate)` with a quantize is clearer and is what every FX library does.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: We moved away from Decimal on purpose in ADR-007 (#112). Everything is int minor units and rounding happens once, in round_half_even_div, so the ledger and the bank agree to the unit. Dan's spreadsheet check is the proof. Introducing Decimal here would reintroduce the int<->Decimal boundary we just removed.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: OK, if finance signed off on the numbers.

threads.rejection_reason: ADR-007: money stays int minor units; round_half_even_div is the single rounding point.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: The first version had `int(amount_cents * 0.005)`. That's float maths on money and it truncates instead of rounding. Please use the helper (`apply_bps(amount_cents, 50)` reads best) or at least integer maths.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Oops, leftover from my prototype. Switched to integer maths with round_half_even_div.
